## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 2: Poisson regression and rate ratios
- Today: when the data are **more variable than a Poisson allows**, which is **usual**
- By the end you can:
  - **measure** overdispersion
  - choose between **quasi-Poisson**, **negative binomial** and **robust SEs**
  - see why **standard errors**, not estimates, are the problem
:::

# Topic 1 — Detecting it {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## The dispersion statistic

::: {.eq}
dispersion = sum of squared Pearson residuals / residual df   (about **1** if Poisson fits)
:::

```{r}
m2 <- glm(cases ~ fogging + slum + rain_lag1 + month_index + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + cos(2 * pi * month / 12) + offset(log(population)), family = poisson, data = dg)
sum(residuals(m2, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(m2)
```

```{r}
check_overdispersion(m2)
```

## What dispersion means

::: {.warn}
A dispersion of **`r round(sum(residuals(m2, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(m2), 1)`** means the Poisson **standard errors are too small by about its square root (`r round(sqrt(sum(residuals(m2, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(m2)), 1)` times)**. The coefficients are still reasonable; the **p-values and CIs are not**.
:::

## Why is count data overdispersed?

::: {.incremental}
- **Unmeasured heterogeneity:** wards differ in ways we did not record
- **Clustering:** events cluster in space and time (outbreaks)
- **Contagion:** one case causes others (not independent)
- **Zero inflation** (Session 4)
:::

# Topic 2 — Three remedies {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Quasi-Poisson

```{r}
m_q <- glm(formula(m2), family = quasipoisson, data = dg)
round(cbind(Poisson_SE = summary(m2)$coefficients[, 2], Quasi_SE = summary(m_q)$coefficients[, 2])[2:3, ], 3)
```

Same **coefficients**, standard errors **multiplied by sqrt(dispersion)**. Simple; no AIC (not a full likelihood).

## Negative binomial

```{r}
m_nb <- MASS::glm.nb(formula(m2), data = dg)
c(theta = round(m_nb$theta, 2)); AIC(m2, m_nb)
```

::: {.eq}
Var(Y) = mu + mu^2^ / theta
:::

::: {.incremental}
- An extra parameter **theta** lets the variance grow **faster than the mean**; **smaller theta = more overdispersion**
- A real likelihood: compare models by **AIC**
- The usual first choice for overdispersed counts
:::

## Rate ratios compared

```{r}
bind_rows(Poisson = tidy(m2, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE), NB = tidy(m_nb, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE), .id = "model") |>
  filter(term == "foggingYes") |> select(model, RR = estimate, low = conf.low, high = conf.high) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

::: {.key}
The **point estimate** barely moves; the **CI is about three times wider** with the negative binomial. Do not report the Poisson CI when the data are overdispersed.
:::

## Robust (clustered) standard errors

```{r}
coeftest(m2, vcov = vcovCL(m2, cluster = dg$ward))[2:3, ]
```

::: {.incremental}
- The same ward appears **36 times**: observations are **correlated**
- `vcovCL(model, cluster = ward)` gives **cluster-robust** standard errors, valid for **correlated** data
- Use with Poisson (rates stay the same, SEs honest) or with NB
:::

# Topic 3 — Choosing {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Which one?

| Option | Use when | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| **Poisson** | dispersion near 1 | rate ratios, AIC |
| **Quasi-Poisson** | overdispersed, only SEs matter | rate ratios, corrected SE, no AIC |
| **Negative binomial** | overdispersed (usual) | rate ratios, AIC, theta |
| **Robust SE** | clustering (repeated wards) | honest SE for any of these |
| Mixed model (random ward effect) | clustering and ward-level heterogeneity | beyond this workshop |

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q1", "A Poisson model has a dispersion statistic of 8. What is the main consequence?",
         c("Standard errors are too small, so p-values are over-optimistic",
           "The coefficients are wrong by a factor of 8 in every model",
           "The model has too few predictors to describe the counts",
           "The offset has been specified incorrectly in the model formula"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Overdispersion leaves the coefficient estimates roughly sensible but understates their uncertainty: the SEs should be inflated by about the square root of the dispersion.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q2", "Which parameter of the negative binomial measures overdispersion?",
         c("theta: the smaller it is, the more overdispersion there is",
           "The intercept of the model, which sets the baseline rate",
           "The offset, because it holds the variance of the counts",
           "The p-value of the dispersion test, which grows with variance"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Variance = mu + mu^2/theta, so a small theta means variance far above the mean and a large theta approaches a Poisson.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q3", "Compared with the Poisson model, what does quasi-Poisson change?",
         c("The coefficients, with the same standard errors",
           "The link function from log to identity",
           "The standard errors, with the same coefficients",
           "The number of observations used"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Quasi-Poisson estimates the dispersion and multiplies the variances by it: coefficients are identical, standard errors are inflated.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q4", "Why use cluster-robust standard errors by ward here?",
         c("The same ward is measured 36 times, so observations are correlated",
           "Wards are too small to be analysed with any count model",
           "Robust standard errors remove overdispersion from the estimates",
           "Poisson models need one single row for each ward in the file"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Repeated months within a ward are not independent, so there is less information than 1,080 independent observations. Clustered SEs account for this.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s3q5", "AIC is 10,745 for the Poisson model and 5,898 for the negative binomial on the same data. What do you conclude?",
         c("The negative binomial fits far better",
           "The two models fit equally well",
           "The Poisson model is better because it has fewer parameters",
           "AIC cannot be compared between these models"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Lower AIC means a better trade-off of fit and complexity. A difference of thousands is overwhelming evidence for the negative binomial.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- Check **dispersion** (about 1 if Poisson); overdispersion is **usual**
- **Negative binomial** (or quasi-Poisson) fixes the SEs; the estimates barely move
- **Clustered robust SEs** for repeated units
- Do not report **Poisson CIs** for overdispersed counts
:::
